messages.text:
Great, 2 follow-up prs:

The new pixel baseline with trimmed end cap and both single/quad modules in the end cap as well.

First PR:
- update the DD4hep model

Second PR:
- update the TDR accordingly
I’ll use the trimmed single/quad endcap as the new baseline, update the DD4hep model in one PR, and carry the resulting geometry and validation into a separate TDR PR.

PR #43 has merged, so I’ll start from that exact trimmed baseline. The Spack preflight still flags changed environment fingerprints; I’ll verify the installed DD4hep, ROOT and Geant4 runtime before using it. The TDR is currently an Overleaf submodule, so I’m also checking how its source changes can be reviewed in the second PR.

The TDR is an Overleaf submodule, which has no GitHub PR interface. Should the second PR contain self-contained TDR source changes in nodd, or target a GitHub TDR mirror?
- Use a nodd PR with self-contained TDR sources
- Use a GitHub TDR mirror (provide the repository)

The installed runtime checks passed: DD4hep 1.38, ROOT 6.40.04 and Geant4 11.4.2 are available. The combined model still exports the older quad-only endcaps, so this needs updates to both the module layout and the support, cooling and service inventories.

I’ll make the TDR changes self-contained in the second nodd PR. The model PR will use the trimmed mixed-module layout as the preliminary default, while preserving the older layouts and their validation evidence.

The selected layout has 2,312 endcap modules and 5,012 active chip areas. I’m carrying its per-disc trimming and radial/tangential orientation into DD4hep, including the retained cooling circuits. The existing coverage gaps and service-packing failures will remain explicit limitations of this preliminary model.

The eight exporter tests passed, including preservation of the barrel and checks against the frozen endcap coordinates. Native DD4hep validation is running now. It checks the material inventory and sensor axes as well as positions, so it can catch orientation errors that matter for non-square pixels.

Native DD4hep validation passed: all 11,806 active areas match, the overlap and material checks pass, and Geant4 initialized successfully. I’m now generating the portable display and retained report. The TDR will distinguish these construction checks from the cooling, routing and coverage qualifications still outstanding.

The TDR will include the trimming schedule, single/quad module counts, support and cooling design, and DD4hep validation results. I’m using the PDF skill to inspect the compiled pages. Since this Mac has no TeX engine, I’ll compile the self-contained sources in the PR’s CI and review the resulting PDF.

The final model workflow passed, including portable display export and Geant4 initialization. The report records an important remaining failure: reference service demand exceeds trunk packing capacity by about 3% and flange-neck capacity by about 40%. The radii remain fixed, so the DD4hep material cells are useful for simulation but do not yet describe a qualified service route.

[PR #44](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/44) is open with the DD4hep model. I’ve created a separate TDR branch stacked on it. Its figures and inventory tables will be generated from the frozen layout and model report, so they stay consistent with the implementation.

The TDR draft and figures are ready for compilation. The chapter explains why the outer discs lose inner rings, preserves the radial/tangential module orientation, and describes the support, cooling and fixed service reservations. Its tables and figure hashes are checked against the frozen reports.

The model PR’s hosted checks passed. The TDR’s first compilation failed, and I’m checking the compiler log before correcting it. I also added a generated barrel inventory table so the chapter documents the full pixel baseline, including the part that remains unchanged.

The compiler failure came from including table rows inside a LaTeX alignment. I’ve changed the generator to emit complete tables and pinned the exact TeX container used by CI. The repaired build is running; once it finishes, I’ll inspect the PDF pages for clipping and unreadable figures.

The repaired TDR compiled successfully: 11 A4 pages, with all references resolved and no overfull text boxes. I’m reviewing the rendered tables and figures now, then I’ll retain the PDF and build evidence in PR #45.

The rendered tables and figures are legible. I caught and corrected a wording error in the model contract: the 4.65 mm thermal depth includes a 4.50 mm core insert and a 0.15 mm skin window. The validated material allocation is unchanged. I’m also keeping the figures from interrupting a module-description paragraph.
The DD4hep update and the self-contained TDR are in separate PRs. I’m checking the final rendered TDR, then finishing the validation records and session log before the final pushes.

The final 11-page TDR compiles cleanly, and I’ve checked every page. I also see that PR #44 has now merged. I’ll put the remaining TDR evidence and shared session closeout in PR #45, and update its base to the branch that received #44.

PR #45 now targets the branch containing the merged DD4hep update. It includes the compiled preview, generated layout tables and figures, and support/cooling/mounting text. The report also retains the unresolved coverage, thermal and service-packing limits.

The preview and session records are ready. The raw TeX log contains trailing whitespace, so I’m retaining it as gzip with hashes for both the compressed file and the original bytes. The PDF and manuscript are unchanged; I’m checking the final push now.

PR #45 is pushed with the reviewed PDF and its source hashes. Its final hosted checks are running. The session logger validates in both checkouts; I’m arranging one follow-up to recover the exact token counters after this turn closes.

The final TDR compilation passed. The DD4hep baseline contains 5,362 modules and 11,806 active chip areas, with native construction, material/identifier checks, overlap checks and Geant4 initialization passing. The hosted regression suite is the last check still running; token recovery is scheduled after this turn closes.
